blocks.text: Reactions of carboxylic acids can be divided into the following types.

items: Reactions involving the acidic hydrogen only.
Reactions involving the replacement of the –OH group.
Those involving the carboxyl group as a whole.

blocks.text: A. Reaction involving acidic hydrogen
Carboxylic acids show considerable acidic character because they give H⁺ ions in water. This why they can react with the basic species and active metals.
a) With active metals
b) With alkalis
c) With metal carbonates and bicarbonates

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The acid in this equation is ethanoic acid, CH₃–COOH; the print shows CH₂. The balanced equation is CH₃–COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃–COO⁻Na⁺ + CO₂ + H₂O.
B. Reactions involving replacement of -OH group
Carboxylic acids can undergo substitution reactions in which the OH group is replaced by some other group like X, OR, NH₂ etc.
a) Reaction with SOCl₂, PCl₃ and PCl₅
b) Reaction with alcohols (Esterification)
Carboxylic acids on heating with alcohols in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid produce esters.

blocks.text_alt: CH₃–COOH (ethanoic acid) + C₂H₅OH (ethanol) ⇌ CH₃–COOC₂H₅ (ethyl ethanoate) + H₂O (H₂SO₄)

blocks.text: C. Reduction involving –COOH group
The powerful reducing agent lithium tetrahydridoaluminate (III) reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols.

blocks.title: Reduction
blocks.text:
i. Gain of H₂ (or H⁻)
ii. Loss of O or O₂
iii. Loss of X₂ (Halogens)
iv. Gain of electrons
v. Decrease in Ox state.
Other common reducing agents H₂/Ni and sodium tetrahydridoborate (III) will not reduce carboxylic acids.
Oxidation of carboxylic acids
Methanoic acid gets oxidized with both weak as well as strong oxidizing agents due to its structure and, hence, acts as a strong reducing agent.

blocks.alt: Methanoic acid, H-C(=O)-OH, drawn twice. On the left the H-C=O part is boxed, with an arrow to 'Aldehydic portion (-CHO) responsible for its behaviour as a powerful reducing agent.' On the right the C(=O)-OH part is boxed, with an arrow to 'Carboxylic portion (-COOH) responsible for its acidic character.'
blocks.caption: The aldehydic and carboxylic portions of methanoic acid (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 111).

blocks.text: Methanoic acid is the only monocarboxylic acid which gives positive silver mirror test (Tollen's test) and brick red precipitates with Fehling's solution. These reactions are used for the identification of methanoic acid.

blocks.title: Oxidation
blocks.text:
1. Loss of H₂ or (H⁻)
2. Addition of O or O₂
3. Addition of X₂
4. Loss of electrons
5. Increase in Ox. State
The oxidation of ethanedioic acid with acidified KMnO₄ or K₂Cr₂O₇ results in the formation of carbon dioxide and water.
